# Tests that pass against a single-node server but FAIL against a cluster.
# The s3tests-cluster workflow honors ../known-failures.txt and ratchets this
# file, so a test that fails on one node and passes on three is not listed
# here.
#
# This is a BUG LIST, not a scope statement. Contrast ../known-failures.txt,
# where an entry means "not implemented / out of scope"; an entry here means
# behaviour that already works on storagefs and does not on the replicated
# data plane. Add one only to unblock CI while a fix is in flight, with the
# root cause and the issue number, and take it out again with the fix.
#
# The 19 entries this file was created with are gone: they were four bugs
# (#98 ranged GET, #99 conditional GET, #100 zero-byte Content-Length,
# #101 chunked PutObject), all fixed. It was empty until the entries below.
#
# --- Default bucket encryption on clusterstore (#124) -----------------------
#
# ?encryption is served by backends that can encrypt, and clusterstore cannot
# yet — the coordinator has to encrypt before it fragments, so that parity,
# repair and peer transfer stay keyless, and that is not built. So it answers
# NotImplemented where storagefs answers the configuration.
#
# The alternative was to let clusterstore *store* a default it cannot honor,
# which would pass these three and produce a bucket configured for an
# encryption that never happens — every write to it refused, or worse,
# accepted in the clear. Failing three tests is the better trade, and it is
# the reason fs.BucketEncrypter is a separate capability rather than another
# method on fs.BucketSettingsStore.
#
# Remove these with clusterstore encryption.
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_delete_bucket_encryption_s3
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_get_bucket_encryption_s3
s3tests/functional/test_s3.py::test_put_bucket_encryption_s3
